# Tool reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_docs.py from the tool definitions. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every tool is read-only (annotated `readOnlyHint: true`, so clients can auto-approve it) and
returns JSON. Dates are in the report timezone (`INSTAGRAM_MCP_TIMEZONE`, else the computer's);
percentages are 0-100.

## Account

### `get_instagram_auth_status`

*Instagram auth status*

Check whether the Instagram server has a working token, which account it reads, which API host it uses, and when the token expires (Instagram Login tokens renew themselves). Call this first if another Instagram tool reports a sign-in problem.

### `get_instagram_profile`

*Instagram profile*

The connected Instagram account's profile and current counts: username, display name, biography, website, followers, following and number of posts. For performance over a period use get_instagram_performance_summary.

## Analytics

### `get_instagram_performance_summary`

*Instagram performance summary*

Account-level totals for a period, like the Insights overview in the Instagram app: views, reach, accounts engaged, interactions (likes, comments, shares, saves, replies, reposts), profile link taps, follows, unfollows and net follows, each with the previous period and % change, plus engagement rate (interactions / reach). Any range up to 2 years; reach and accounts_engaged need a range of 29 days or less (unique accounts can't be added up). For trends use get_instagram_metrics_over_time; for posts get_instagram_top_media.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `period` | `last_7_days` \| `last_14_days` \| `last_28_days` \| `last_30_days` \| `last_90_days` \| `last_180_days` \| `last_365_days` \| `this_month` \| `last_month` \| `this_year` \| `last_year` \| `all_available` \| null | `"last_28_days"` | Named date range. Rolling ranges end yesterday (the latest complete day) in the report timezone; Instagram keeps account insights for 2 years ('all_available'). Ignored when start_date is set. |
| `start_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range start, YYYY-MM-DD (at most 2 years back). Overrides `period`. |
| `end_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range end, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to yesterday; today gives a partial day. |
| `compare_to_previous` | boolean | `true` | Also read the previous period of equal length and compute % change. |
| `include_breakdowns` | boolean | `true` | Add totals by content type (reel, post, carousel, story) and views/reach from followers vs non-followers. |

### `get_instagram_metrics_over_time`

*Instagram metrics over time*

A time series of account metrics by day, week or month, for trend analysis and growth charts (views, reach, interactions, likes, comments, shares, saves, follows, unfollows, net follows, …). One Instagram request per bucket: use week or month for long periods. Buckets cut off by the range are flagged partial=true.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metrics` | list[`views` \| `reach` \| `accounts_engaged` \| `interactions` \| `likes` \| `comments` \| `shares` \| `saves` \| `replies` \| `reposts` \| `profile_link_taps` \| `follows` \| `unfollows` \| `net_follows`] \| null | `null` | Metrics per bucket. Default: views, reach, interactions, follows, unfollows. |
| `granularity` | `day` \| `week` \| `month` | `"day"` | Bucket size. Weeks run Monday to Sunday. |
| `period` | `last_7_days` \| `last_14_days` \| `last_28_days` \| `last_30_days` \| `last_90_days` \| `last_180_days` \| `last_365_days` \| `this_month` \| `last_month` \| `this_year` \| `last_year` \| `all_available` \| null | `"last_28_days"` | Named date range. Rolling ranges end yesterday (the latest complete day) in the report timezone; Instagram keeps account insights for 2 years ('all_available'). Ignored when start_date is set. |
| `start_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range start, YYYY-MM-DD (at most 2 years back). Overrides `period`. |
| `end_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range end, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to yesterday; today gives a partial day. |
| `include_follower_total` | boolean | `false` | Add followers_end per bucket: the follower count at the end of each bucket, estimated backwards from today's count (for growth charts). |
| `save_to` | string \| null | `null` | Optional file to also save the rows to (.csv or .json). A bare filename goes in the output directory (INSTAGRAM_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR); absolute paths are allowed. |

### `get_instagram_audience`

*Instagram audience*

Who the audience is: age, gender, age × gender, top cities and top countries of the followers, or of the accounts that engaged with the content. Rows have counts and share_pct; age also has app_share_pct (the app's own rule) and gender share_of_known_pct.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `breakdown` | `age` \| `gender` \| `age_gender` \| `city` \| `country` | **required** | age, gender, age_gender (both together), city or country (top 45). |
| `audience` | `followers` \| `engaged` | `"followers"` | 'followers' = who follows the account (a snapshot, like the app's audience view); 'engaged' = accounts that interacted with content during the timeframe. |
| `timeframe` | `this_week` \| `this_month` | `"this_month"` | Window for the engaged audience (Meta's own: the current week or month). |
| `limit` | integer | `45` | Maximum rows for city and country. |

### `get_instagram_online_followers`

*Instagram online followers*

When followers are on Instagram: average followers online per hour of the day, and the best weekday + hour slots, in the report timezone. Use it to pick posting times.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `days` | integer | `28` | Days to average over (Meta keeps 30). |

## Posts, reels and stories

### `list_instagram_media`

*List Instagram posts*

List the account's posts and reels (newest first) with caption, type, publish time, permalink, likes and comments; optionally with each post's lifetime insights and an embedded thumbnail. Covers the whole history, not just two years. For a ranking within a period use get_instagram_top_media; stories are in list_instagram_stories.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `published_after` | string \| null | `null` | Only posts published on/after YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `published_before` | string \| null | `null` | Only posts published on/before YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `media_type` | `reel` \| `image` \| `video` \| `carousel` \| `feed` \| null | `null` | Only reels, images, videos, carousels, or 'feed' (everything except reels). |
| `caption_contains` | string \| null | `null` | Case-insensitive caption filter. |
| `sort_by` | `newest` \| `oldest` \| `most_viewed` \| `most_reach` \| `most_interactions` \| `most_liked` \| `most_commented` \| `most_shared` \| `most_saved` \| `highest_engagement` \| `longest_watch_time` | `"newest"` | Order. Sorting by a performance metric reads each post's insights (slower). |
| `limit` | integer | `50` | Maximum posts to return. |
| `include_insights` | boolean | `false` | Add each post's lifetime insights: views, reach, interactions, saves, shares, reposts, follows (feed posts), watch time and skip rate (reels), engagement rate. |
| `include_thumbnails` | boolean | `false` | Embed each post's image as a ~5 KB WebP data URI (up to 60 posts). |
| `save_to` | string \| null | `null` | Optional file to also save the rows to (.csv or .json). A bare filename goes in the output directory (INSTAGRAM_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR); absolute paths are allowed. |

### `get_instagram_media_insights`

*Instagram post insights*

Every lifetime metric Meta has for specific posts, reels or stories: views, reach, likes, comments, shares, saves, reposts, interactions, engagement rate; follows, profile visits and profile activity for feed posts; average and total watch time and skip rate for reels; replies and navigation for stories.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `media_ids` | list[string] | **required** | Up to 50 media IDs (from list_instagram_media). |

### `get_instagram_top_media`

*Top Instagram posts*

Rank the posts published in a period by a lifetime metric (views, reach, interactions, saves, shares, engagement rate, average watch time, …), with all their insights. Also returns how many posts were published in the period.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metric` | `views` \| `reach` \| `interactions` \| `likes` \| `comments` \| `shares` \| `saves` \| `reposts` \| `follows` \| `engagement_rate_pct` \| `avg_watch_time_s` | `"views"` | What to rank by. |
| `limit` | integer | `10` | How many posts. |
| `period` | `last_7_days` \| `last_14_days` \| `last_28_days` \| `last_30_days` \| `last_90_days` \| `last_180_days` \| `last_365_days` \| `this_month` \| `last_month` \| `this_year` \| `last_year` \| `all_available` \| null | `"last_90_days"` | Named date range. Rolling ranges end yesterday (the latest complete day) in the report timezone; Instagram keeps account insights for 2 years ('all_available'). Ignored when start_date is set. |
| `start_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range start, YYYY-MM-DD (at most 2 years back). Overrides `period`. |
| `end_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range end, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to yesterday; today gives a partial day. |
| `media_type` | `reel` \| `image` \| `video` \| `carousel` \| `feed` \| null | `null` | Only reels, images, videos, carousels, or 'feed'. |

### `list_instagram_stories`

*Instagram stories*

The account's current stories (published in the last 24 hours) with their insights: views, reach, replies, shares, interactions, follows, profile visits and navigation (taps forward/back, exits, swipes). Meta doesn't give access to expired stories.

### `list_instagram_comments`

*Instagram comments*

Read comments (username, text, time, likes) on one post or across the latest posts, e.g. to summarise sentiment, find questions or content ideas. Needs the comments permission on the token (instagram_manage_comments or instagram_business_manage_comments).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `media_id` | string \| null | `null` | Comments on one post. Omit for comments on the latest posts. |
| `posts` | integer | `10` | Without media_id: how many of the latest posts to read. |
| `limit` | integer | `100` | Maximum comments to return. |
| `include_replies` | boolean | `false` | Include replies under each comment. |
| `save_to` | string \| null | `null` | Optional file to also save the rows to (.csv or .json). A bare filename goes in the output directory (INSTAGRAM_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR); absolute paths are allowed. |

### `list_instagram_tagged_media`

*Posts tagging the account*

Public posts by other accounts in which the connected account is tagged (newest first), with owner, caption, likes and comments: useful to track mentions, collaborations and UGC.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer | `25` | Maximum posts to return. |

## Other accounts

### `get_instagram_public_account`

*Public Instagram account*

Public profile and recent posts of another Business or Creator account (followers, posts, bio, and per post likes, comments and reel views), for benchmarking against peers or vetting partners. Needs a unified login or Facebook Login token.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `username` | string | **required** | Another Business or Creator account's username, e.g. 'nasa'. |
| `media_limit` | integer | `12` | Recent posts to include (0 for the profile only). |

## Reports and raw access

### `get_instagram_report`

*Instagram report*

Everything about the account for a period in one stable JSON snapshot (schema_version 1): profile, performance totals vs the previous period (with content-type and follower splits), follower audience (gender, age, top 10 cities and countries), every post published in the period with its lifetime insights, and the best hours to post. Sections Instagram can't provide are null or empty and explained in `unavailable`; the call still succeeds. Shape: docs/report.md.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `period` | `last_7_days` \| `last_14_days` \| `last_28_days` \| `last_30_days` \| `last_90_days` \| `last_180_days` \| `last_365_days` \| `this_month` \| `last_month` \| `this_year` \| `last_year` \| `all_available` \| null | `"last_28_days"` | Named date range. Rolling ranges end yesterday (the latest complete day) in the report timezone; Instagram keeps account insights for 2 years ('all_available'). Ignored when start_date is set. |
| `start_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range start, YYYY-MM-DD (at most 2 years back). Overrides `period`. |
| `end_date` | string \| null | `null` | Custom range end, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Defaults to yesterday; today gives a partial day. |
| `include_thumbnails` | boolean | `false` | Embed each post's image as a small WebP data URI (~5 KB per post). |
| `save_to` | string \| null | `null` | Optional .json file to also save the report to. |

### `query_instagram_api`

*Raw Instagram API query*

Run any read-only GET on Meta's Instagram Graph API for the connected account and return Meta's raw JSON: the escape hatch when no other tool fits. Account insights allow at most 30 days between since and until (Unix seconds) and go back 2 years. Pagination: pass 'after' from paging.cursors. Meta's error message is returned if a request is invalid.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | **required** | Graph API path, relative: 'me' is the connected account, e.g. 'me/insights', 'me/media', '<media-id>/insights', '<media-id>/children'. |
| `params` | object \| null | `null` | Query parameters, e.g. {'metric': 'views,reach', 'period': 'day', 'metric_type': 'total_value', 'since': '1730000000', 'until': '1732000000'}. |
